summary.title: Use The Index, Luke
summary.one_liner: A free web edition of a book on SQL indexing and tuning for developers, covering how indexes work and how to write queries that use them across major SQL databases.
keywords: join types nested loops hash join sort-merge
how to make sql queries faster
takeaways: How B-tree indexes are structured (balanced tree with a doubly linked list of leaf nodes) and why that matters for lookups.
Why certain WHERE clause patterns (functions, obfuscated conditions, LIKE with leading wildcards, type mismatches) make indexes slow or unusable.
How column order in concatenated indexes affects equality, range and ORDER BY use.
How joins (nested loops, hash, sort-merge) and pagination methods (offset vs seek) interact with indexing.
Vendor-specific notes are provided for Db2, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL and SQL Server.
summary.summary: Use The Index, Luke is a free web edition of the author's book SQL Performance Explained, aimed at developers rather than database administrators. It is vendor-agnostic in its main text, with product-specific notes for Db2 (LUW), MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL and SQL Server, and lists the versions tested. The table of contents walks from index anatomy and B-tree structure through WHERE clause patterns, joins, sorting and grouping, pagination, and the effect of indexes on DML statements. The page itself is an index of topics rather than a full tutorial, so the details are in the linked chapters.
